segments.opening_question_spark: If pressure crushes trapped air, why doesn't it crush your whole body?
segments.entry_transition: Most of your body is water, and water barely compresses.
segments.body_01: Water-rich tissue changes very little under pressure.
segments.body_02: Air in your ears and sinuses shrinks much more.
segments.body_03: Pressure rises about one atmosphere every ten meters.
segments.body_04: At ten meters, total pressure is about double.
segments.body_05: Unequal pressure can injure those air-filled spaces.
segments.body_06: Breathing underwater would remove the limit of running out of air.
segments.body_07: But it would not remove pressure from your body.
segments.body_08: At extreme depths, high pressure can disturb normal nerve function.
segments.body_09: So breathing alone does not set one fixed human depth.
segments.optional_closing: Breathing solves one limit, but pressure creates others.

issues.quote: Water-rich tissue changes very little under pressure.
issues.problem: “Water-rich tissue” is an academic-sounding phrase that may slow first-listen understanding.
issues.suggestion: Body tissue that contains a lot of water changes very little under pressure.

issues.quote: Most of your body is water, and water barely compresses.
issues.problem: “Compresses” is less familiar than a plain description of what happens.
issues.suggestion: Most of your body is water, and water hardly gets squeezed smaller.

issues.quote: Pressure rises about one atmosphere every ten meters.
issues.problem: “One atmosphere” is a technical pressure unit, but the sentence does not explain what it means.
issues.suggestion: Pressure rises by about the pressure of the air at the surface every ten meters.

issues.quote: Unequal pressure can injure those air-filled spaces.
issues.problem: It sounds as if the empty spaces themselves are injured, which makes the physical effect harder to picture.
issues.suggestion: Unequal pressure can injure your ears and sinuses.

issues.quote: At extreme depths, high pressure can disturb normal nerve function.
issues.problem: “Disturb normal nerve function” is formal and abstract for spoken B1 English.
issues.suggestion: At extreme depths, high pressure can stop nerves from working normally.

issues.quote: So breathing alone does not set one fixed human depth.
issues.problem: “One fixed human depth” is an unusual phrase and makes the conclusion less immediate on first listen.
issues.suggestion: So breathing alone does not set one fixed limit on how deep humans can go.

notes: The opening question is concrete and easy to follow, and it keeps the same promised idea as the reference.
The main scientific meaning is preserved: underwater breathing removes the air-supply limit but does not remove pressure-related limits.

segments.opening_question_spark: If water crushes air pockets, why not your whole body?

segments.body_01: Body tissue with lots of water barely changes.
segments.body_02: Air in your ears and sinuses shrinks much more.
segments.body_03: Every ten meters, pressure rises by about the air pressure at the surface.
segments.body_04: At ten meters, total pressure doubles.
segments.body_05: Unequal pressure can injure your ears and sinuses.
segments.body_06: Breathing underwater removes the problem of running out of air.
segments.body_07: But pressure would still affect your body.
segments.body_08: At extreme depths, high pressure can stop nerves from working normally.
segments.body_09: So breathing alone does not set a fixed depth limit.
segments.optional_closing: Breathing solves one limit, but pressure creates others.

issues.quote: At ten meters, total pressure doubles.
issues.problem: The reference says total pressure is about double. Removing "about" turns an approximate value into an exact one.
issues.suggestion: At ten meters, total pressure is about double.

issues.quote: At extreme depths, high pressure can stop nerves from working normally.
issues.problem: "Stop nerves from working normally" can sound stronger than the reference claim that high pressure can disturb normal nerve function.
issues.suggestion: At extreme depths, high pressure can disturb how nerves normally work.
